verdict.tagline: Complex mechanical depths meet persistent technical instability in the endgame.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep character building and complex passive trees
you are willing to use external guides for learning
not_for_you_if: you need stable performance during intense endgame combat
you want rewarding ground loot without relying on specific mechanics
you are discouraged by brutal early game difficulty spikes

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering frequent bugs, crashes, and phase-locked map bosses during recent leagues.

citations.review_text:
I've run face first into several bugs and QoL nightmares this league that are apparently bugs that have been around for several leagues. Nightmare Map bosses getting phase locked be that by fates or otherwise, TWO spectres being deleted by some mechanic that we weren't able to ascertain, and some of the worst UI/UX decisions when it comes to AG gearing and Spectre management. 

Combining this with the issues that came about post Settlers league, I certainly wouldn't recommend the game in it's current state. It feels like excess dev time has been pushed towards features with good bones, but not enough has been put into fixing existing issues. Basic bugs that are a landmine to the avg player's experience.
Constant crashes and bugs. GGG let's everyone BETA test their game every league.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that regular ground loot drops feel unrewarding, requiring players to rely heavily on specific mechanics for good items.

citations.review_text:
This is my favorite game of all time. Wish my first review was a positive review, because overall it still is a great game. I'm leaving a bad review for this current league and the direction of the game.

The newest league shows they don't really know what they're doing. Evident in the latest mid-league patch. They acknowledged that ground loot still wasn't where it needed to be, and that players wanted more "tinks" (rare drops), so they just added 2 new uninspiring currency items to the drop pool and moved several league-specific ones to the core pool. Which contradicts the whole "philosophy" they've had going on of separating drops so they only come from their specific leagues. 

All in all the game lost its charm in terms of player agency and how we want to play with the variety of content. Scarabs were a annoying as hell to buy and organize but the gameplay they allowed was fun. Threads seems like a better idea on paper but I'm way more worried about how long it'll take to make them actually feel good because they're such a drastic change, than I would be if they just reverted back to the old system.

This league mechanic is also very half-baked. Somehow it feels too quick and too tedious at the same time. Like it's rewarding enough to interact with it, doesn't take a long time to do, but it's just not fun enough to feel good taking 10 seconds to get more drops. Other than clicking buttons on the screen a few times to pick rewards you literally just kill some monsters around the pot and then kill the boss. Even torchlight I feel would have a mechanic like this. a loop of simple interactions, but then they'd eventually lead to a longer, fun interaction, then start over (like twinightmare)

review for 3.30

I’ve been playing Path of Exile for years, and it’s one of the games I’ve always come back to every league. But for the past few leagues, the game just hasn’t felt as exciting as it used to, and 3.30 hasn’t changed that for me.

My biggest problem is ground loot. Killing monsters and clearing maps should feel rewarding, but most of what drops is useless, and the good stuff only comes from very specific mechanics and strategies. It takes away the fun of just playing the game and getting a surprise drop. After all the talk before launch about reworking loot, I was hoping this would finally be the league that fixed it, so it’s very disappointing to see ground loot still feeling this bad.

I still love this game and I want it to do well, which is why I’m writing this. GGG, please fix the ground loot. Make regular drops worth picking up again and bring back that excitement that kept so many of us playing for years.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as extremely complex and difficult to learn without external resources like YouTube guides, community assistance, or help from experienced friends.

citations.review_text:
What made me stay is the depth. No other game has this much going on under the hood.

The crafting is basically gambling, but gambling you can make as deterministic as possible, and when it hits, the dopamine is insane. The grind is real, but it's actually rewarding. Your hours feel like they matter because you're constantly progressing your character, your gear, your understanding of the game.

I've played a lot of builds, and that's the point. The build variety is massive and the fun really comes from individual preference. There is a playstyle for literally everyone. The game feels really, really hard at first because you have to fight so many systems at once, but once you understand how every little detail works, it's extremely rewarding.

The endgame is huge, the variety in playstyles and league mechanics is huge, but what keeps the game alive are the seasonal league changes. Every league feels fresh again.

Worst part? Dying and not understanding your mistakes, and grinding for hours and hours when you don't know what to do. That almost made me quit. What saved it was trading, YouTube guides, and the community. The community is great. A lot of people will actually help you if you send them your PoB.

I'd recommend this to people who like strategy, depth, and a community that works together on metas and stuff. I would NOT recommend it to people who want quick dopamine. Everything needs grind and understanding. You can't just turn your brain off until endgame farming, in my opinion.

If you like to obliterate every monster on your screen in seconds, this game is for you.

Very fun game that is also horribly obtuse. It took a ton of hand holding from friends who have played this game for thousands of hours for me to even start to understand it, and I'm just scratching the surface. Excellent monetization system. No real complaints though, given that it's a free game.
